title: Supply is elastic, installment #1637 - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: An AER paper by Jakobsen, Kleven, Kolsrud, Landais and Munoz using Scandinavian administrative data finds a 1pp rise in the top wealth-tax rate cuts the stock of wealthy taxpayers ~2% via emigration, but aggregate economic effects are small.

insights.claim: Scandinavian administrative data show a 1 percentage point increase in the top wealth tax rate reduces the stock of wealthy taxpayers by about 2 percent through international migration.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Wealth-tax revenue estimates must account for meaningful tax-base flight among the rich.
insights.quote: A 1 percentage point increase in the top wealth tax rate decreases the stock of wealthy taxpayers by about 2 percent.
insights.locator: Using administrative data from Scandinavian countries

insights.claim: Cowen frames the finding as another instance of 'supply is elastic' — the supply of wealthy taxpayers responds to taxes.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Policy that assumes an immobile tax base overstates revenue.

insights.claim: A large fraction of the wealthy who emigrate are business owners, and their businesses are negatively affected by the owner's out-migration.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Wealth taxes can hurt firm-level performance via owner departure, not just revenue.
insights.locator: Using administrative data from Scandinavian countries

insights.claim: Despite the migration, aggregate effects of a 1pp top wealth-tax rise are modest: employment falls 0.02%, investment 0.07% and value added 0.10%.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Macro costs of wealth taxes appear small, complicating both pro- and anti-wealth-tax arguments.
insights.quote: reduce employment by 0.02 percent, investments by 0.07 percent, and value added by 0.10 percent
insights.locator: Using administrative data from Scandinavian countries
